log: LOOP 216 -- WHAT IS COMPARED AGAINST WHAT, AND CAN ANY MODEL BEAT THE MEASUREMENT NOISE?
K1 THE DATA DICTIONARY
RAW: A549 lung adenocarcinoma, 100 nM dexamethasone, ENCODE polyA RNA-seq.
TPM matrix (56, 58735) = (samples, genes); 16 timepoints, replicates [1, 2, 3, 4]
GRID USED: [30, 60, 120, 180, 240, 420, 480, 600, 720] minutes -- the 9 points where replicates [1, 2, 3] all exist and t >= 30
TARGET m(t,g) = mean over replicates r of
[ log2(1 + TPM(t,g,r)) - log2(1 + TPM(30,g,r)) ]
EACH REPLICATE IS BASELINE-SUBTRACTED AGAINST ITS OWN t=30 BEFORE AVERAGING.
That order matters and is deliberate: averaging TPM first and taking one log
lets a replicate entering or leaving the series shift the level, which is the
defect that put a batch step at t=30 in loop 191 and made every half-time
28 minutes (loop_response_timing_d.py:302-317). My first statement of this
dictionary had the order wrong and K1 caught it at 8.53e-01.
SET POINT S(g) = mean of m over the last three grid points (480, 600, 720 min).
FORWARD TARGET dm(t,g) = m(t,g) - m(t_prev,g). THIS is what persistence predicts
as zero and what every R2 since loop 198 is computed on.
INPUTS, per gene, all measured BEFORE or independently of the target:
chip     9 ENCODE A549 ChIP/DNase tracks x 3 summaries = 27 columns
gains    200 Perturb-seq CRISPRi signatures, K562 = 200 columns
physics  879 JASPAR motifs x 3 chemical potentials = 2,637 columns
independent recomputation of m from raw TPM: max abs difference 0.000e+00

K5 PASS -- the plateau is measurable at R2 0.834 while a single interval is at -0.540. The problem is the DIFFERENCING, not the data: averaging three timepoints keeps the signal and cancels the noise, subtracting two adjacent ones cancels the signal and keeps it
K6 WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW
A replicate ceiling assumes the replicates are independent measurements of the same
quantity. ENCODE isogenic replicates share library prep and batch, so they
UNDERSTATE the true noise and the real ceiling is lower than measured here.
The ceiling is for the target AS DEFINED -- a difference of two three-replicate
means. A different target definition, such as a fitted trajectory slope, would have
a different and probably higher ceiling, and that is the constructive reading.
Nothing here says the models are good. It says the target they were scored on may
not have been predictable, which is a different and more useful claim.
